plan: In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid regardless of how high I bid above my value, and bidding above my value only risks winning when I'd have negative profit. Bidding below my value only risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, my optimal bid equals my private value of $9.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others bid. If I bid exactly my value ($40), I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I pay that second-highest price - guaranteeing non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if others bid high; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With no prior history to adjust for, truthful bidding is optimal.

This is a second-price auction with private values. In this format, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding above value risks paying more than value; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. With no history to adjust for opponents' behavior, I'll bid exactly my value of $32.
